dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: Sept 7: Starship Flight 14 Vehicles Enter Final Checkout as Sept 15 Orbital Attempt Nears
heroSubtitle: 8,890 days since SpaceX founding — Ship 41 and Booster 21 have finished their required single-vehicle tests and moved into final checkout in Starbase's Mega Bays ahead of Starship Flight 14, SpaceX's first attempt at a full orbital insertion; next up is loading the Starlink V3 payload into Ship 41 before rollout and stacking, with the Sept 15 no-earlier-than date still an unofficial planning-slide target. That follows a Sept 3-4 FAA Finding of No Significant Impact clearing added Pacific Ocean contingency splashdown zones for Ship 41, and a next-generation Ship 42 completing cryogenic proof tests at Massey's on Sept 3 ahead of a later flight. On the launch side, SpaceX flew the Starlink 15-24 mission from Vandenberg on Sept 6 (B1088, 19th flight, 27 satellites) — the year's 80th Starlink mission and 103rd Falcon 9 launch of 2026 — following the Sept 2 Starlink 15-23 flight (B1063, 35th flight) that pushed the 2026 Falcon-family tally to 104-105 launches depending on source. SPCX investors are now watching Sept 9, the next scheduled insider share-unlock tranche (~319M shares) under the company's staggered post-IPO lockup schedule.
